recentItems.title: Fatal shooting in Punchbowl was a targeted attack, police say | ABC NEWS
recentItems.description:
A man shot dead in the car park of a community centre in Sydney's south-west has been confirmed as boxing coach Louis Meehan.
Police believed the 32-year-old had links to outlaw motorcycle gangs and that the shooting was a targeted attack.
It marked the third fatal shooting in Sydney in just over a week.
Police said the attack in Punchbowl had no connection to a gangland war linked to the previous two incidents.

recentItems.description:

But this isolation also has its challenges. Women across the Top End's rural area came together recently to forge new friendships swap ideas and offer support through difficult times. Felicity James has this report for ABC News Northern Territory.

recentItems.description:
The NT's Deputy Chief Minister has defended his decision not to publicly disclose a family link to a gas-powered data centre granted rights to government land.

recentItems.title: Rib contouring surgery raises ethical concerns in Australia | ABC NEWS
recentItems.description:
Experts are warning social media promotion of a new rib contouring surgery could fuel pressure to achieve extreme body shapes.

The procedure involves reshaping the ribs to create a smaller waist and has gained popularity among influencers.

The Australian Society of Plastic Surgeons says complications can include a collapsed lung (pneumothorax) and haemothorax, where blood pools between the chest wall and lungs. It says these complications have occurred in about one in 5,000 patients.

The ABC does not suggest companies or people promoting the surgery are breaking the law.

Reporting by Shari Hams

recentItems.title: Markets pricing in longer US-Iran war following conflict escalation, says Kyle Rodda | The Business
recentItems.description:
A dramatic escalation in shipping attacks in the Middle East war has reverberated through global markets.

The latest tit-for-tat strikes on tankers have pushed the oil price above $US100 a barrel and wiped tens of billions of dollars off the value of the ASX on Thursday.

Capital.com's Kyle Rodda says the markets are pricing in a more protracted war, where there are going to be periodic flare-ups. 

Investors hoping for an imminent exit ramp have been disappointed by President Donald Trump's latest timeline for the conflict, when he said he thinks "the war is going to end immediately after the election...because they can't hold out any longer."

Meanwhile, the bond market also continues to flash red. The yield on the US 10-year Treasury bond has risen to a three-year high of 4.86 per cent in protest over US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's attempt to push down rates, with a $US6 billion bond buyback.

Kyle Rodda joined The Business from London. He and host David Taylor also discuss the new Apple foldable phone - which has a a $3,499 price tag - and what that means for the company and its new boss, John Ternus' reputation.

recentItems.title: Inflation fears drag ASX to seven-week low, oil jumps above $US100 | Finance Report | ABC NEWS
recentItems.description:
The Australian share market wiped out all its gains since late July after the benchmark oil price, Brent crude, surged above $US100 per barrel.
The latest escalation in US-Iran hostilities is raising concerns the war will drag on beyond the US mid-term elections in November, which will likely keep inflation higher for longer. 
There is a high likelihood the European Central Bank (ECB), Bank of Japan (BoJ), US Federal Reserve and Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) will lift interest rates in response to the inflationary pressures.

Presented by David Chau.
